original_query: SELECT t0.SAL FROM (SELECT EMPNO, ENAME, JOB, MGR, HIREDATE, SAL, COMM, SLACKER, SAL AS SAL0, SAL = 4 AS f9 FROM EMPNULLABLES WHERE DEPTNO = 20 AND SAL > 1000) AS t0 INNER JOIN (SELECT t2.SAL, t5.SAL AS SAL0, t5.f9 FROM (SELECT EMPNO, ENAME, JOB, MGR, HIREDATE, SAL, COMM, SLACKER FROM EMPNULLABLES WHERE DEPTNO = 20 AND SAL > 1000) AS t2 INNER JOIN (SELECT SAL, SAL = 4 AS f9 FROM EMPNULLABLES WHERE DEPTNO = 20 AND SAL > 1000 GROUP BY SAL, SAL = 4) AS t5 ON t2.SAL = t5.SAL OR t5.f9 GROUP BY t2.SAL, t5.SAL, t5.f9 HAVING t5.SAL = t2.SAL) AS t8 ON t0.SAL = t8.SAL0 AND t0.f9 = t8.f9
rewritten_query:
SELECT SAL
FROM EMPNULLABLES
WHERE DEPTNO = 20
  AND SAL > 1000;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The derived expression `SAL = 4 AS f9` is always FALSE because the filter requires `SAL > 1000`. Therefore `OR t5.f9` and `t0.f9 = t8.f9` are always false constant conditions and can be removed.

The t8 derived table (t2 JOIN t5 GROUP BY ... HAVING) collapses to `SELECT DISTINCT SAL` of the same filtered set, since t5 is just distinct SAL (with constant false f9) and the join/HAVING equate the same SAL.
The outer join between t0 (all filtered rows) and t8 (distinct SAL of the same filtered rows) matches every t0 row exactly once and does not filter or duplicate rows, so the entire join is redundant.

Replace the whole query with a single scan: `SELECT SAL FROM EMPNULLABLES WHERE DEPTNO = 20 AND SAL > 1000`. Given the table has ~45M rows while ~55 rows match, an index on `(DEPTNO, SAL)` is recommended.
Retain only the essential predicates `DEPTNO = 20 AND SAL > 1000`; all other conditions, grouping, and self-joins are redundant.
